# BMad project context: set up, adopt, refresh or audit repo agent instructions (short pointer)

Curated by Skill Harbor — a short pointer to @bmad-code-org's bmad-project-context workflow: a conversation that produces a repository's agent instructions as a small verified block inside `AGENTS.md`. The user brings governance/security/standards rules, the repository supplies the rest — verified, never guessed. Five intents: setup (greenfield), adopt (existing instruction file without a managed block), refresh (managed block exists — diff against the recorded SHA), record (capture one observed agent mistake as a pitfall), and audit (re-verify every caveat and path, shrink or prune). The core loop: assess and report against `references/best-practices.md` with a ledger entry per existing instruction (retain/rewrite/relocate/automate/delete with reason, evidence and approval flag); ask the user for outside documents; discover and verify by scanning configs/CI/source rather than asking; interview only the gaps (recall questions, batches of at most eight, never ask what a scan could answer); show the complete block plus the settled ledger before writing; splice between markers; close with what went in, what was left out and why. Rules: no writes until step 5, show the block before writing it, never commit, deletions need one of four grounds. Honest caveats: **no license declared in the repository manifest — license unknown**, so this is a short fiche linking to the source, without reusing its content; designed to run inside a BMad project (`_bmad/` folder) though usable...
